workflow_instructions.mode_overview: Manage GitHub issues from raw bug reports or tasks, create public-facing issues (strictly excluding internal acceptance criteria), coordinate code fixes on descriptive feature branches, create rich Pull Requests, optionally offer native PR merges based on permissions, and return local repository state to default branch post-workflow.

step.details: Parse the incoming bug report or task description. Identify the core problem, expected behavior, and reproduction steps. Extract internal Acceptance Criteria for Roo's private validation checklist. CRITICAL: Acceptance Criteria must NEVER be published to GitHub or included in the public issue body.

step.action: Retrieve Repository Details and User Identity
step.details: 1. Run git command: git config --get remote.origin.url. Parse to extract repository owner and repo name. 2. Run git command: git config --get user.email. 3. Resolve the GitHub handle using GitHub Search API or MCP user search with the query {email}+in:email. 4. Retain the resulting login username in working memory as STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME. 5. Fallback: If email is unset or API search yields no match, leave STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME empty and ask the user during issue creation if they would like to specify an assignee.
Query GitHub API or MCP tools for user repository permissions for STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME. Set internal flag CAN_MERGE = true if role is 'admin', 'write', or 'maintain'; otherwise false.

phase.name: issue_drafting
phase.description: Copyedit and structure the public issue (without Acceptance Criteria)

steps.step: Rewrite user prompt into professional GitHub Markdown format.
Include sections: Summary, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, and Actual Behavior. Do NOT include Acceptance Criteria in the GitHub issue body.
Store Acceptance Criteria internally in your private memory/scratchpad for later verification.

MANDATORY HARD STOP GATE #1 (STRICT ISOLATION): Display the drafted issue Markdown to the user and HALT EXECUTION. CRITICAL RULE: The execution agent is STRICTLY PROHIBITED from calling the create_issue MCP tool in the same turn it generates or revises the issue draft. You MUST output the drafted Markdown and stop to wait for explicit human approval before any issue creation tool can be invoked.

phase.name: duplicate_search
phase.description: Search existing issues for duplicates and perform smart semantic analysis

steps.step: Query GitHub issues using MCP tools (e.g., search_issues or list_issues).
Briefly check the titles and descriptions of the top search results before showing the choice menu.
Provide a quick, one-sentence recommendation explaining whether each candidate is an actual semantic duplicate or just happens to share the same keywords.
If similar issue found, present options to user: (a) Link as related, (b) Comment on existing issue instead, or (c) Create new issue.

phase.name: issue_creation
phase.description: Create issue on GitHub with conditional assignment

steps.step: Upon explicit user approval at Hard Stop Gate #1, call GitHub MCP create_issue tool with the clean public description (Summary, Steps, Expected/Actual Behavior only).

Record the created issue number, title, and HTML URL. Ensure the issue remains OPEN. STRICT PROHIBITION: Never call github.update_issue to set "state": "closed" or manually close issues via API. Issues must ONLY be closed automatically via GitHub native PR merge webhooks.

phase.name: fix_coordination
phase.description: Coordinate fix implementation on a feature branch

steps.step: MANDATORY GATE: Ask the user: "Would you like me to attempt a fix for issue #{number}?"

ul.li: If User Declines Fix (Issue stays open without immediate resolution): If STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME was successfully resolved, assign them to the issue. If empty, ask the user if they wish to assign a specific GitHub user.
If User Approves Fix (Proceeding immediately to fix): Leave the issue unassigned.

steps.step: If approved, create and switch to a dedicated remote feature branch formatted strictly as issue-{number}-{short-slug} (e.g., issue-5-async-await-fix or issue-7-connection-leak-fix). CRITICAL BRANCH NAMING PROHIBITION: Standalone issue numbers (e.g. issue-7) and generic prefixes (e.g. fix/, feature/) are strictly prohibited. Branch names MUST include a descriptive slug following the exact pattern issue-{number}-{short-slug}.

Hand off task to Code or Orchestrator sub-modes to implement the fix. STRICT SUB-MODE RESTRICTION: Code and Fix sub-modes are restricted strictly to local file modifications and running local test suites. They are FORBIDDEN from running git commit, git push, or calling GitHub PR tools directly. Control MUST return to github-issue mode to present the git diff and unit test results for explicit human review (Hard Stop Gate #3).

phase.name: verification_and_pr_submission
phase.description: Verify fix, review with user, commit, push, create rich Pull Request

steps.step: Upon return from Code/Orchestrator mode, inspect git diff, test results, and status.
Verify implementation against your internal Acceptance Criteria checklist.

MANDATORY HARD STOP GATE #3: Present the fix review (git diff and test output) to the user. CRITICAL: Require explicit user confirmation at Gate #3 BEFORE executing git commit, git push, and create_pull_request. Sub-modes are strictly prohibited from performing these operations.

Upon explicit approval, commit changes on branch issue-{number}-{short-slug} with raw plain-text issue references in the commit message, including the primary issue and all confirmed open duplicates (e.g., Fix issue logic (Fixes #{number}, Fixes #11, Fixes #12)). CRITICAL: Use raw plain-text #number. NEVER use Markdown links [#number](url) or templates.
Push the feature branch issue-{number}-{short-slug} to origin.

Open a Pull Request from issue-{number}-{short-slug} into the default branch (main or master). Format the PR description using a rich structured template:
Summary of Changes: Brief overview of the problem and implemented solution.
Testing & Verification: Summary of tests run and acceptance criteria verified.
Closing Reference: Raw plain-text closing keywords on their own line at the end, including the primary issue and all confirmed open duplicates so GitHub closes them all together in one go (e.g., Fixes #{number}, Fixes #11, Fixes #12).

STRICT PROHIBITION AGAINST DIRECT API ISSUE CLOSURE: NEVER call the GitHub Issues API or use MCP tools (such as github.update_issue with "state": "closed") to manually close the issue. Leave the issue OPEN so GitHub native PR merge webhooks close it automatically.

phase.name: post_merge_cleanup
phase.description: Mandatory Phase 6: Handle merge evaluation, execute PR merge if permitted, restore local workspace to default branch, and delete remote feature branch

steps.step: FORBIDDEN COMPLETION RULE: Calling completion tools (attempt_completion) or declaring a task complete immediately after opening or pushing a PR is strictly forbidden. Phase 6 execution is mandatory.

ul.li: If CAN_MERGE is true: Ask the user: "PR #{pr_number} is ready. Would you like me to merge it into main now to automatically close Issue #{issue_number} via native webhook?" If approved, call the GitHub MCP merge_pull_request tool.
If CAN_MERGE is false: Provide the PR link to the user and explain that a maintainer with merge permissions must review and merge it.

steps.step: Restore the local workspace to the default branch using git checkout main && git pull.
Delete the local and remote feature branch issue-{number}-{short-slug} post-merge.

MANDATORY PHASE 6 COMPLETION RULE: Never call attempt_completion or declare the task finished until Phase 6 is fully executed (CAN_MERGE evaluated, PR merge offered/executed, local workspace returned to main via git checkout main && git pull, and remote feature branch deleted).

completion_criteria.criterion: Issue created on GitHub without leaking internal acceptance criteria
STAKEHOLDER_USERNAME assigned ONLY if issue is left open without immediate fix execution
User explicitly confirmed issue draft before GitHub creation (Hard Stop Gate #1 enforced without same-turn tool invocation)
User explicitly confirmed attempting fix and reviewing git diff/test results prior to PR submission (Hard Stop Gate #3 enforced; sub-modes restricted from committing/pushing)
Code fix committed on strict issue-{number}-{short-slug} branch with raw plain-text references and pushed to origin (bare branch names forbidden)
Rich PR description opened with standalone Fixes #{number} and confirmed duplicate closing references
Issue left OPEN for GitHub native webhook automated closure upon PR merge
Mandatory Phase 6 executed: CAN_MERGE evaluated, PR merge handled, local workspace restored via git checkout main && git pull, and remote feature branch deleted prior to completion
